content.comment_body: Hello all, I discovered a useful resource for studying communication protocols of [product_name] under the setup directory Program Files\[company_name]\[product_name]_V5\lib\classes.jar. I have extracted and decompiled several Java classes, such as ByteWriteListener.class, DataTransfer.class, PortNotAvailableException.class, TransmissionFailedException.class, and VirtualDeviceDataTransfer.class. Through these classes, I learned how [product_name] software interacts with the device by observing their function calls. I used Eclipse and JDK, importing classes.jar into the build path, and developed a sample test program for [article_no]. I managed to start and stop [product_name], but now I am working to control DI/DO, AI, AO, Flags, and Set/Actual values. Once complete, I’ll share the full source code here. For now, I've attached the decompiled classes and the original class.jar files. If interested in collaborating, please let me know. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Forum members are reverse engineering communication protocols for [product_name] using custom Java applications to enable direct interaction and automation. Some have succeeded in basic device control via serial and Ethernet communication, but users face compatibility challenges, especially with different Windows versions, highlighting the need for adequate permissions and dependencies. The thread shows active collaboration and information exchange, but a universally working, cross-platform solution is still pending.
analysis.user_expectations: Users seek reliable, documented ways to programmatically control [product_name] using custom Java code, expecting protocol clarity and broad compatibility with major Windows versions. They hope for simple dependency management and smooth interoperability between official software and their custom applications.
